research_question: How does full-call Q.ANT CPU-backend numerical error scale with input-channel count and Fourier-component count when no split-call reconstruction is used?
observations: Exp020 showed increasing full-call Q.ANT-versus-exact-cosine error as tensor size and component count increased.
At 32 inputs and 10 outputs, increasing from 4 to 8 Fourier components approximately doubled the measured error.
Split-call diagnostics themselves accumulate numerical differences, so Exp021 will use only one full Q.ANT call per condition.
hypothesis: Mean absolute Q.ANT-versus-exact-cosine error will increase systematically with the number of accumulated terms, input_channels multiplied by components, and a simple power-law model will explain a substantial fraction of the variation.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if error is not monotonically related to accumulated-term count across repeated seeds or if fitted scaling against term count has poor explanatory power relative to separate input/component effects.

scaling_analysis: log-log slope of MAE versus accumulated_terms
separate grouped summaries by input_channels and components

limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Synthetic random amplitudes/phases do not reproduce the learned parameter distribution of FashionMNIST models.
A fitted scaling law is descriptive over the tested range and should not be extrapolated beyond it without validation.
